subject: EdgeGrid discovery — agreed goals, SLOs, and ops checklist
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@edgegrid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Jun 2029 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeGrid discovery — agreed goals, SLOs, and ops checklist

Hi Lena / Marco —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the immediate next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of the problem you described
- Primary product: real-time recommendations + short personalization snippets inside search results.
- Current pain: latency spikes during promotions, high p95 tail for short responses, and unpredictable unit cost as model traffic grows.
- Data constraints: production data cannot leave your VPC for compliance — procurement asked about an on-prem / VPC option.

Goals we aligned on
- Latency: p95 inference <= 300ms for generation responses up to 40 tokens (goal: 250ms where possible).
- Throughput: sustain 200 QPS steady-state with 2x headroom during promotional bursts (~400 QPS).
- Cost: lower per-request cost vs current managed endpoint by 20–35% through batching, KV cache, and quantization.
- Operational controls: clear autoscale and fallback so product degrades gracefully (fallback to cached responses or smaller model).

Technical constraints you flagged
- Model choices: want an open-weight LLM (13–30B class preferred) with ability to run int8/quantized variants.
- Response size: typical generation 20–40 tokens, but streaming for longer follow-ups.
- Security: SOC2 evidence + ability to route traffic via a VPC/private deployment.

Immediate recommendations (high level)
- Deployment topology to validate in PoC: Redwood Dedicated reserved pool in us-west (customer-dedicated GPUs) with a VPC private control plane for audit/logging. Autoscale burst policy to cover 400 QPS.
- Runtime config: aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeat users; continuous batching with max latency budget 50ms for builder batch windows; fall back to a 7B quantized variant for requests that approach latency SLO when capacity constrained.
- Model & quantization: test 13B FP16 baseline + int8 quantized 13B for cost/latency tradeoffs. Measure accuracy delta on your evaluation prompt set.

Attached: short throughput/latency scan we ran during the call (edgegrid_throughput-latency-scan.pdf) and a rough topology sketch (edgegrid_topology-sketch.drawio).

Next steps / mutual action plan
1) You: share the short eval prompt set & 250 sample production traces (anonymized) — procurement indicated a secure shared Drive link is fine.
2) Redwood: schedule a focused technical deep-dive (engineers only) to align on kernel selection, batching windows, and warm-up strategy (we propose Thurs 6/6, 10am PT).
3) Redwood: provide an initial cost/latency estimate and two PoC topology options (Hosted+Dedic hybrid vs Private/VPC) within 48 hours post-deep-dive.
4) Procurement: share procurement timeline and any required security docs — we’ll prep SOC2 artifacts and a short data flow diagram for legal.

Please reply with any corrections and whether 6/6 10am PT works for your engineers.

Thanks —
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Lead, Solutions Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Lena Park <lena@edgegrid.ai>

Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco@edgegrid.ai>, EdgeGrid Procurement <procure@edgegrid.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Jun 2029 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeGrid discovery — agreed goals, SLOs, and ops checklist

Sofia —

Thanks for the crisp recap, looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 200 QPS steady-state was an average across three traffic regions; primary region for PoC is us-west. We can provide traces scoped to us-west only.
- For model selection: we want to avoid any >30B models for cost reasons; 13B with safe-response filtering is our preference.
- SOC2: procurement asked specifically for retention window options and whether logs can be forwarded to our Splunk instance. Can you confirm?

6/6 10am PT works for our infra + ML engineer (Marco) — thanks for proposing.

We’ll upload 250 anonymized traces to the Drive folder you linked by EOD Wed.

—Lena

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@edgegrid.ai>, Marco Ruiz <marco@edgegrid.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Jun 2029 17:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeGrid discovery — agreed goals, SLOs, and ops checklist

Lena / Marco —

Great — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive (so the call can focus on knobs and measurements):

1) Latency and batching tradeoffs - For your target p95 <= 300ms on ~32-token responses, our experience is:
  * Single-request path (no batching) on H100-backed Dedicated pods: p95 ≈ 120–200ms for a well-optimized 13B int8 run (depends on sequence length).
  * With continuous batching turned on (batch windows up to 30ms) we can increase throughput ~2–3x at the expense of ~30–40ms added tail. We will propose a conservative 30ms batching window to balance utilization and latency.

2) Throughput sizing (PoC baseline) - You said 200 QPS steady-state with 2x burst headroom. For a 13B int8 variant, rough sizing for baseline:
  * Reserved capacity: 8 x A100/H100-style GPUs (Redwood Dedicated units) to hit ~200 QPS with tail margins, depending on prompt distribution.
  * Burst policy: autoscale + burst buffer to 16 GPUs for promotional events (target warm-up < 60s).
  * KV cache: prefix caching anticipated to drop per-request compute by ~30% for returning users — strongly recommended.

3) Failure / fallback strategy - Canary + fallback plan we recommend:
  * Canary rollout: start 2 GPUs serving 10% traffic, monitor p95, CPU throttling, error rates.
  * Fallback: route to cached responses or a quantized 7B model when 95th crosses SLO. We’ll include an automated circuit-breaker in the proposal.

4) Security and logging - Yes, logs and audit events can be forwarded to your Splunk collector via secure tunnel (we will share the connector config). Retention windows are configurable per deployment — default 90 days, can be reduced to meet your compliance ask. For Private/VPC deployments, no data exits your network control plane by default.

5) What we’ll bring to the 6/6 deep-dive
  * Kernel/cuda optimization notes and expected p50/p95 numbers for FP16 vs int8 on common sequences.
  * A short runbook for warm-up and autoscale triggers (warm start, cache priming).
  * Cost/latency table for the two topology options (Dedicated reserved vs Private VPC).

Attachments included: edgegrid_throughput-latency-scan.pdf (short sampling we ran in the call), topology sketch, and a draft mutual action plan (mop_edgegrid_mutual_action_plan.md).

If you can drop the traces and a short eval prompt set to the Drive folder, we’ll pre-run a small accuracy/latency delta test on both FP16 and int8 13B variants and share results in the deep-dive.

See you Thursday; I’ll send the calendar invite with a technical agenda and pre-reads.

Cheers,
Priyom
